site_note: V2 item 5.3 (two primaries): only on a Case File linked to the same patient's other Case File, and only for histopathology, cytology, IHC and molecular records: among several candidates for one record, or several documents carrying a required value, one that names another protocol's site and not this one steps aside and is named on the row for review; a document naming no site never does, and when every candidate names another site every candidate stays. Organ words only. A preference, never a filter; a patient with one cancer is checked as before.
note: DRAFT, not approved for real use: needs a clinician's check. Configurable by the clinical team. Required records transcribed from the NCG Guidelines for Gynaecological Cancers (2019) (National Cancer Grid, India), the endometrial cancer section (the investigation algorithm and the summary table of imaging and management recommendations: Essential (a), Optimal (b), Optional (c)), each with its verbatim quote under where (the Word file has no page numbers). Tiers printed by NCG are kept; the tiers whose tier_basis says 'proposed' or 'proposal' (clinical_history, her2) are proposals, to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). A record NCG gives only under a condition the system never judges (an age, a finding, a plan) is shown with NCG's own tier and the condition, never counted. Uterine sarcoma and carcinosarcoma are not separate in the book (carcinosarcoma is grouped with the Type II histology) and are not covered here. The book's algorithm for advanced disease says PET-CT should not be done in early lesions. The FIGO stage is the stage as recorded by the clinician, never computed. Nothing here suggests treatment.
settings_note: Setting of the Case File, chosen by the clinician from what the signed reports record (the system never computes stage). The two settings follow the book's investigation algorithm, 'Clinically early stage' and 'Advanced stage' (the summary table splits disease confined to the body of the uterus, Stage II, Stage III and Stage IV).
